name: Pelatiah
title: Prince in Israel who died during Ezekiel's prophecy
summary: Pelatiah, son of Benaiah, was one of the twenty-five princes in Israel whom Ezekiel saw in a vision at the east gate of the Lord's temple. He gave the people evil counsel and became a symbol of Jerusalem's ungodly leadership. During Ezekiel's prophecy, he fell dead, confirming God's judgment against the false advisors.

keyEvents.title: The Vision of the Twenty-Five Princes
keyEvents.description: In a vision, Ezekiel was brought to the east gate of the Lord's temple, where he saw twenty-five men, including Pelatiah son of Benaiah and Jaazaniah son of Azzur, who were princes among the people.

keyEvents.title: Evil Counsel to the People
keyEvents.description: Pelatiah and the other princes gave evil counsel in Jerusalem. They encouraged the people with false security, saying that the city was the pot that protected them, like meat in a pot.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on the Leaders
keyEvents.description: The Lord commanded Ezekiel to prophesy against these princes and declared that He knew their thoughts and evil plans, and that He would judge them.

keyEvents.title: Pelatiah's Sudden Death
keyEvents.description: While Ezekiel was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah fell dead. This was a powerful sign of God's judgment on Jerusalem's ungodly leaders and shocked the prophet Ezekiel.

keyEvents.title: Ezekiel's Reaction and Intercession
keyEvents.description: When Pelatiah died, Ezekiel fell on his face and cried out loudly to the Lord: 'O Lord God! Will you make a complete end of what remains of Israel?' The prophet feared total destruction of the people.

keyEvents.title: God's Promise of Restoration
keyEvents.description: After Pelatiah's death, God answered Ezekiel's cry for help with a promise that he would gather the people of Israel again, give them one heart and a new spirit, and remove the heart of stone from their bodies.
